title: The sky didn’t just darken.
paragraphs:
The sky didn’t just darken.
It exploded.

Ice the size of stones.
Fire flashing through the storm.
Thunder tearing the heavens open like a warning from eternity.
Egypt had never seen anything like it.
And neither had the world.
This was the 7th plague.

Not random weather.
Not natural disaster.
Not coincidence.
Judgment.
But hidden inside the thunder was a whisper of mercy.
Let me show you.
Pharaoh had heard the warning again and again.
“Let My people go.” — Exodus 9:13

But pride is stubborn.
Power is intoxicating.
And a hardened heart does not listen easily.

Egypt had already seen the Nile turn to blood.
They had endured frogs, gnats, flies, livestock death, and painful boils.
Yet Pharaoh refused to bow.
So God escalated the warning.
Through Moses, the Lord spoke:

“Send therefore now, and gather thy cattle, and all that thou hast in the field… for upon every man and beast which shall be found in the field… the hail shall come down upon them, and they shall die.” — Exodus 9:19
Did you catch that?
Before the storm came…
God warned them.
Judgment was coming — but mercy opened the door first.
And then the sky broke.
“And the LORD sent thunder and hail, and the fire ran along upon the ground… so there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous.” — Exodus 9:23–24
Imagine it.
Hailstones crashing like falling boulders.
Lightning ripping across the sky like burning spears.
Fire dancing through the storm.

Fields shattered.
Trees ripped apart.
Livestock collapsing in the open fields.
Egypt’s gods of sky and weather were silent.
Powerless.
Because this storm was not about climate.
It was about authority.
God was revealing a truth Pharaoh refused to accept:
The Lord alone rules heaven and earth.
But here is the part that should stop us cold.
Some Egyptians listened.
Scripture says:
“He that feared the word of the LORD among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his cattle flee into the houses.” — Exodus 9:20

Those who believed the warning…
were spared.

Those who ignored it…
suffered loss.

Same storm.
Different outcomes.
The difference?
Whether they feared the Word of the Lord.
The hail devastated Egypt.
But in the land of Goshen—where the Israelites lived—
there was no hail.
Not one stone.
Not one flame.
God was drawing a line in the storm.

Protection for His people.
Judgment for rebellion.
Finally Pharaoh cracked.
He called for Moses and Aaron and said:
“I have sinned this time: the LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.” — Exodus 9:27
For a moment, it sounded like repentance.
But it wasn’t.
Because when the storm stopped…
Pharaoh’s heart hardened again.
He wanted relief.
Not transformation.
He wanted the pain gone.
But not God as Lord.
And that’s the uncomfortable mirror.
How many people cry out to God only during the storm?
“Lord help me!”
“Lord save me!”
“Lord I’ll change!”
But when the thunder fades…
So does the promise.
Pharaoh’s story is not just ancient history.
It is a warning.
Because the Bible teaches something even more sobering.
The plagues of Egypt were shadows.
Foreshadows of a greater judgment coming upon the world.
The book of Revelation describes hail, fire, and divine wrath again falling upon the earth (Revelation 16).
History is moving toward a final moment when God will confront evil fully.
But just like in Egypt—
Mercy comes first.
And that mercy has a name.
Jesus Christ.
At the cross, the storm of judgment fell.
But it did not fall on us.
It fell on Him.
Jesus bore the wrath our sins deserved so that anyone who repents and trusts in Him can receive forgiveness, restoration, and eternal life.
Not because we earned it.
But because grace stepped into the storm.
The 7th plague teaches something unforgettable:
God warns before He judges.
God calls before He condemns.
God opens a door before the storm arrives.
The question is not whether the warning exists.
The question is whether we will listen.
Because just like the Egyptians who ran their animals inside—
those who take God at His Word find refuge.
So if this message found you today…
Don’t harden your heart like Pharaoh.
Don’t wait for the next storm to take God seriously.
Turn to Christ.
Run to the refuge while mercy still calls.
Because the same God who sent the hail…
also sent a Savior.
And His grace is stronger than any storm.
If this message moved you, share it so someone else can hear the warning and the hope.
Someone out there is standing in the field while the clouds are gathering.
And they need to know there is still time to run inside.
“He who feared the word of the LORD… fled into the houses.” — Exodus 9:20
Choose wisely.
Choose Christ.
